calls.title: PhonePe / GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting focused on resolving issues with GrowthBook's incremental load logic, particularly the misalignment between partitioned data and timestamp ordering. Luke Sonnet and Jinan Sarmadi discussed potential solutions, including shifting to partition-based incremental loads to enhance data accuracy during reloading and deduplication processes. Device-generated timestamps were also noted as problematic, creating noise in data correctness, leading to an agreement on minimal filtering for incremental loads. The integration of AI assistance in the GrowthBook application was highlighted as a priority for improving user support, while upcoming discussions will refine data handling and performance metrics. Overall, participants committed to follow up on proposed solutions and keep communications active for swift resolutions.
calls.keywords: Incremental load, timestamp filtering, data partitioning, GrowthBook, PhonePe, ETL processing
calls.action_items:
**Luke Sonnet**
Discuss with GrowthBook team and provide a plan/ETA by next morning for adapting incremental load logic to rely on serial partition loading instead of timestamp filtering (09:00)
Explore quick fix removing timestamp filters in ETL queries while considering constraints on future timestamps (15:00)
Arrange subsequent meetings to advise PhonePe on dimension setup for improved performance (23:25)

**Jinan Sarmadi**
Conduct experiments testing full load vs incremental load with filtered partition timestamp data and report results back (04:50)
Confirm that both exposure and metric tables will have timestamp filtering removed for incremental load as suggested (16:00)

**Koushik Roy**
Confirm internal data processing excludes future timestamps and rely on partition-based filtering (18:40)
Provide any additional context or feedback to GrowthBook team to minimize back-and-forth and align assumptions (14:50)
